subject.title: fix(ui): persist Control UI settings across reconnects via gateway-owned LWW prefs writes

question: Should OpenClaw make `ui.prefs` a gateway-enforced leaf-level last-writer-wins exception to the normal whole-document `config.patch` CAS contract?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and concurrency-policy change, not only a local UI repair; the gateway boundary determines its long-term behavior for all callers.

options.title: Approve bounded LWW contract
options.body: Accept hash-free leaf writes only under `ui.prefs`, subject to current-head real-gateway proof and normal merge refresh.

options.title: Keep universal document CAS
options.body: Retain strict CAS for all configuration patches and pursue a different UI-side conflict/replay design.

options.title: Narrow the preference API first
options.body: Introduce an explicit gateway preference-write operation rather than changing `config.patch` semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded LWW contract
recommendation.body: Accept hash-free leaf writes only under `ui.prefs`, subject to current-head real-gateway proof and normal merge refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The available PR and related-PR history makes steipete the clearest current routing candidate for the proposed ownership boundary.
